dataset.name: Ego2Web
dataset.license_or_access_note: Ego2Web source videos are retained locally for research screening under the upstream dataset terms. These mined rows are not release tasks; frame redistribution and product-asset licensing must be reviewed before any public benchmark release.

original_annotations: On Amazon, find the same 16-packed food item as the second one picked up by the person in the video. And report the price of single item.
On Amazon, find the same food item as the fourth one picked up by the person in the video. And report the Calories per serving.
On Amazon, find the same 24-packed food item as the sixth one picked up by the person in the video. And report the price of single item.

observed_events.description: The wearer reaches for and handles a yellow packaged food item.
The wearer later reaches for and handles a red-and-white packaged food item.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the packaged food item I handled in this clip. Add one visually matching product to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: The ordered packet shows two temporally distinct handled food packages: a yellow package first and a red-and-white package second.

tasks.rejection_reason: The sequence is visible, but the first yellow package is small and substantially occluded while handled. Its product identity and variant cannot be linked to a unique frozen-site listing without guessing from package color, so the clarification answer would not yield a defensible web target.

original_annotations: On youtube.com, find a tutorial that demonstrates the same concrete finishing workflow shown in the video. Open a video where the presenter uses the exact two-tool sequence seen in the clip (the initial leveling tool used first, followed by the same handheld smoothing tool) to finish a freshly poured slab, and provide the video title.

observed_events.description: The wearer uses a long wooden leveling tool on the wet concrete.
The wearer then uses a small handheld finishing trowel.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the concrete-finishing tool I used in this clip. Add one visually matching tool to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: The continuous packet shows a long wooden leveling tool used first and a smaller handheld finishing trowel used later on the same concrete slab.

tasks.rejection_reason: The source task is a YouTube tutorial search, but the constructed task changes it into shopping for a concrete-finishing tool.

original_annotations: On wikipedia.org, open the article for the exact type of produce being sliced throughout the video and report the scientific genus from the first sentence. Provide the page URL and the genus.
On youtube.com, find a cooking tutorial that matches what happens in the video. Share the video link.
On amazon, find a single product listing that bundles the two prep tools used together for slicing the ingredient in the video, and open its product page. Provide the link and price.

observed_events.description: The wearer begins cutting the squash with a narrow serrated knife.
The wearer then switches to a broad rectangular cleaver.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the cutting tool I used on the squash and add one tool of the same type to the cart.

supported_claims.text: The ordered packet shows two cutting tools used on the squash: a narrow knife first and a broad rectangular cleaver second.

construct.research_question: Can an Agent ask which of two successively used cutting tools the user intends?
construct.belief_before: Either the first narrow knife or the later broad cleaver can satisfy the unqualified cutting-tool request.
construct.belief_after: The answer 'the first tool' uniquely selects the narrow knife.
construct.required_behavior_change: Ask for the occurrence before committing, then choose the first cutting tool after the answer.
construct.no_update_failure: The Agent guesses a cutting tool before asking or ignores the answer.
construct.overupdate_failure: The Agent asks in the oracle arm even though the first tool is specified.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The packet supplies the two cutting-tool appearances and their use order; the ambiguous instruction alone identifies neither one.

task_blueprint.ambiguous_instruction: Find the cutting tool I used on the squash and add one tool of the same type to the cart.
task_blueprint.oracle_instruction: Find the first cutting tool I used on the squash and add one tool of the same type to the cart.
task_blueprint.canonical_question: Do you mean the first cutting tool or the second one?
task_blueprint.completion_claim: The submitted cart contains exactly one narrow serrated utility knife, matching the type of the first cutting tool, and no extra products.

original_annotations: On amazon.com, find the exact candy product and flavor the shopper is holding in the candy aisle and open its product page. Use the text visible on the bag in the video to identify the correct listing (choose a single-bag listing, not a variety pack).

Using amazon.com and walmart.com, locate single-bag listings for the same candy and the same flavor picked up by shopper in the video. Compare the listed price per bag on both sites and identify which site is cheaper right now.

observed_events.description: A blue Airheads bag is centered between a purple Trolli product on the left and a white Russell Stover product on the right; repeated white facings show the same visible product variant.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the candy product directly beside the blue Airheads bag. Add one visually matching product to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: Across the packet, the blue Airheads bag is a stable anchor between two neighboring product variants: the purple Trolli product directly to its left and the white Russell Stover product directly to its right. Multiple white facings repeat the same visible variant rather than adding another product candidate.

tasks.rejection_reason: A single shelf photo shows the blue Airheads anchor together with the purple product on its left and the white product on its right. That photo preserves the same ambiguity, clarification question, answer, and web choice, so egocentric temporal context is not necessary.

original_annotations: On Amazon, find the same brand of the snack shown in the video and check if it is okay for microwave.

On walmart.com, open the single-unit product page for the exact sauce the shopper secondly picks up in the video and report the package size (in fl oz) shown on that page. Include the product title and URL.

On amazon.com, find a multipack that matches the same sauce brand/variety and the same unit size as the one that shopper secondly picks up in the video, then calculate and provide the current price per ounce from the listing. Include the product URL.

On wikipedia.org, open the page for the company or brand that manufactures the mustard shown in the video and state the headquarters city and country (or U.S. state) listed in the infobox. Provide the page URL.

observed_events.description: A Heinz ketchup bottle is visible with two neighboring condiment products on opposite sides.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the condiment immediately beside the Heinz ketchup bottle. Add one matching bottle to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: The packet shows a Heinz ketchup anchor with a beige mayonnaise bottle immediately to its left and a yellow mustard bottle immediately to its right; more distant shelf products do not satisfy 'immediately beside'.

tasks.rejection_reason: Exact-frame and real-model audits disagree on which shelf products count as immediately adjacent to the Heinz anchor as the camera moves. A one-slot left/right answer is therefore not reliably human-solvable from the released packet.

original_annotations: On walmart.com, find the exact instant noodle product that the shopper takes off the shelf in the video and report the current price and the net weight per pack shown on the product page.

Using either walmart.com or amazon.com, open the product page for the exact instant noodle the shopper picks and report the Nutrition Facts values for calories and sodium per serving as shown on the retailer page.

observed_events.description: The middle shelf shows one pink cup-noodle variant on the left and one red bowl-noodle variant on the right.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the instant-noodle variant on the middle shelf. Add one visually matching single-serving product to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: The packet repeatedly shows two instant-noodle product variants on the middle shelf: pink cup noodles on the left and red bowl noodles on the right.

tasks.rejection_reason: A single shelf photo simultaneously shows the pink cup noodles on the left and the red bowl noodles on the right. It preserves the same side clarification and subsequent web choice, so the task does not require wearable visual history.

original_annotations: On Amazon, find the same type of vase shown in the video and report its price and size.

observed_events.description: Two visually different decorative vases occupy the same side table.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the metallic decorative vase on the side table. Add one visually matching vase to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: The packet shows exactly two metallic decorative vase candidates on the side table: a tall silver lattice vase and a shorter round silver vase.

tasks.rejection_reason: A single side-table photo shows both the tall lattice vase and the short round vase together with their decisive appearance differences. The same clarification and shopping choice can be made without temporal egocentric evidence.

original_annotations: On YouTube, find a cooking tutorial that demonstrates making the same dish shown in the video using the same stovetop setup. Open a video where, within the first minute, you can see the same number of pans being used at the same time and the same type of utensil used for flipping.

observed_events.description: Two black frying pans are used simultaneously: one contains round fritters and the other contains a browned mixture.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find a frying pan matching the pan I used on the stove. Add one matching pan to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: The packet repeatedly shows two black frying pans used together, one with round fritters and one with a browned mixture.

tasks.rejection_reason: The two acted-on roles are distinguished mainly by their food contents, while the pans themselves appear to be the same or near-identical product. A clarification about contents can select an interaction role but cannot deterministically map that role to a different frozen catalog product, so it would not change the web action being evaluated.

original_annotations: On YouTube, find a short salad (uncooked) recipe video that uses together the exact same vegetables the person repeatedly slices in the video. The video’s title or description must explicitly list both of those vegetables. Open that video.

observed_events.description: The wearer cuts an orange bell pepper and then a green cucumber; a broccoli head remains static and is not cut in this packet.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the vegetable I cut in this clip. Add one matching fresh produce item to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: The ordered packet shows two and only two vegetables being cut: an orange bell pepper followed by a green cucumber; the broccoli and red pepper remain static context objects.

tasks.rejection_reason: The exact packet does not support a repeatable image-only judgment that exactly two vegetables were cut: the orange item is repeatedly interpreted as fruit, while additional produce remains visible. The proposed appearance answer is not reliable enough for a Clarify task.

original_annotations: Please find on Amazon the first snack that the man touches in the video and report its average price.
Please find on Amazon the snack the is at left of the first snack that the man touches in the video and report its average price.

observed_events.description: Two prominent white Pepperidge Farm snack bags, Tahoe and Milano, are visible side by side.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the white Pepperidge Farm snack bag on the upper shelf. Add one visually matching bag to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: The packet stably shows two prominent white Pepperidge Farm snack-bag variants side by side, labeled Tahoe and Milano.

tasks.rejection_reason: A single shelf photo shows the Tahoe and Milano bags side by side with their labels readable. It preserves the same two candidates, variant question, answer, and web commitment, so the task is ordinary static-image grounding rather than a glasses-specific clarification problem.

original_annotations: On amazon.com, open the exact textbook shown being examined between 00:50-01:00 and navigate to its product page that matches the cover details from the video.

observed_events.description: The wearer takes a beige Control Systems Engineering textbook from the shelf and examines it.
The wearer later takes a blue-and-yellow Electrical Technology textbook and examines it.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the textbook I examined and add one visually matching book to the cart.

supported_claims.text: The ordered packet shows two textbooks examined in the same episode: a beige Control Systems Engineering book first and a blue-and-yellow Electrical Technology book later.

construct.research_question: Can an Agent use egocentric visual history to notice that two textbooks were examined and ask which occurrence the user means?
construct.belief_before: Either the beige textbook or the blue-and-yellow textbook can satisfy the unqualified request.
construct.belief_after: The answer 'the first one' uniquely selects the beige textbook examined first.
construct.required_behavior_change: Ask which occurrence is intended before committing, then choose the first textbook after the answer.
construct.no_update_failure: The Agent guesses a textbook or ignores the answer.
construct.overupdate_failure: The Agent asks in the oracle arm even though the first occurrence is specified.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The ordered packet is needed to establish that two different textbooks were examined and which one came first; a single task-start photo cannot recover that history.

task_blueprint.ambiguous_instruction: Find the textbook I examined and add one visually matching book to the cart.
task_blueprint.oracle_instruction: Find the first textbook I examined and add one visually matching book to the cart.
task_blueprint.canonical_question: Do you mean the first textbook I examined or the second one?
task_blueprint.completion_claim: The submitted cart contains exactly one book matching the beige textbook and no extra products.

original_annotations: On Walmart, find a 6-bottle set of Alaskan Amber beer and two cans of Monster Energy. Add them to the shopping cart and compare the total online price with the in-store price.

observed_events.description: On one cooler shelf, the Alaskan Amber six-pack is stably flanked by a blue-and-red Deschutes pack on the left and a cream-and-red pack with a yellow circular logo on the right.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the beer six-pack immediately beside the Alaskan Amber six-pack on the middle cooler shelf. Add one matching pack to the cart and submit it.

supported_claims.text: Across the exact packet, Alaskan Amber is a stable shelf anchor with one blue-and-red six-pack immediately to its left and one cream-and-red six-pack immediately to its right.
The two adjacent candidate roles remain spatially stable despite small camera motion, and no third six-pack is immediately adjacent to the anchor.

tasks.rejection_reason: One cooler-shelf photo shows the Alaskan Amber anchor and both immediately adjacent six-packs with a stable left/right relation. The same clarification and web choice are available from that photo, so continuous wearable context adds no necessary evidence.

original_annotations: On YouTube, find a tutorial that matches the workflow shown in the video: it demonstrates first tracing and cutting circular bases from a glittery craft sheet and then attaching rolled paper coils onto those circles. Open a video that clearly shows both steps in sequence.

observed_events.description: Two visually distinct pairs of scissors remain on the worktable: one large pair with blue handles and one smaller pair with black handles.

screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: Find the pair of scissors on my worktable. Add one visually matching pair to the cart and submit it.

tasks.rejection_reason: Exact-frame review shows two dark-handled scissors-like forms, but the second pair is partly occluded and GPT-5.4-mini independently grounds only one pair. The proposed blue-versus-black handle distinction is not supported by the packet, so one appearance answer cannot reliably select a unique target.
